summary.headline: An excellent business, but the price is about 75% above what it's worth
summary.text: Dialog Axiata (DIAL.N0000) is Sri Lanka's dominant telecom company: about 64% of mobile users, the largest broadband and pay-TV operator, the first 5G network, low debt and a AAA local credit rating. Results are strong: nine-month EPS Rs 3.10 against Rs 1.62, trailing EPS about Rs 3.74, borrowings down to Rs 64bn. This full redo re-read the 2025 annual report and the June and September 2026 interims, recorded the capex, depreciation and working-capital figures that were missing, and applies the new required-return rule: a beta of 0.63 gives a cost of equity of 14.7% (was a hand-set 16.5%) and a WACC of 13.8%. The DCF now values the whole company at WACC and subtracts net debt. Fair value rises from Rs 25.50 to about Rs 28.70, mainly because of the lower discount rate. At Rs 50.20 (CSE close, 13 November 2026) the price is about 75% above that; it implies a WACC of about 10%, below the 12.24% government bond. I'd buy at up to about Rs 24.40 and treat under Rs 21.50 as a strong buy. The business tests still pass 3 of 4, so it stays on the watch list. The beta is provisional: Damodaran's emerging-markets figure couldn't be read in this run.

quality.reason: Dominant, cash-generative and lightly indebted; the one failure is the 2022 loss in the rupee crisis. Re-scored 14 November 2026 from the re-read reports: unchanged.

highlights.title: What changed in this full redo (14 November 2026)
highlights.text: Requested as /redo DIAL full. The 2025 annual report and the June and September 2026 interims were re-read from the CSE downloads. New in the record: 2025 depreciation, impairment and amortisation Rs 48.2bn, capex booked Rs 27.5bn, working capital up Rs 18.3bn, operating profit Rs 38.6bn, tax rate 22.2%, interest paid Rs 8.6bn (inside operating cash flow), and the same for 2024. Discount rates now come from a beta of 0.63 (cost of equity 14.7%, WACC 13.8%) instead of a hand-set 16.5%, and the DCF values the whole company less net debt. Fair value Rs 25.50 → Rs 28.70.

highlights.title: September 2026 quarter (reviewed by the auditors)
highlights.text: Revenue up 6.2% to Rs 48.54bn; profit up 62% to Rs 9.24bn (EPS Rs 1.00 against Rs 0.62). Gross margin 58.4% (53.6%) as direct costs fell 5%; finance costs fell 42% to Rs 1.91bn, offset partly by a Rs 0.92bn exchange loss.

highlights.title: Nine months to September 2026
highlights.text: Revenue up 8.2% to Rs 144.1bn; operating profit Rs 39.3bn against Rs 27.6bn; profit Rs 28.5bn against Rs 14.9bn (EPS Rs 3.10 against Rs 1.62). Operating cash flow Rs 67.1bn (Rs 50.6bn); interest paid fell to Rs 4.2bn (Rs 6.6bn). Effective tax rate 14.4%.

highlights.title: Stronger balance sheet
highlights.text: Borrowings fell to Rs 64.1bn from Rs 76.5bn in December (Rs 107.7bn at end-2024); cash Rs 20.6bn. Net debt including leases is Rs 56.7bn, 0.62x equity and 0.58x EBITDA. NAV per share rose to Rs 9.99 even after Rs 26.7bn of dividends.

highlights.title: Where the depreciation goes
highlights.text: The Rs 48.2bn charged in 2025 is equipment depreciation Rs 31.8bn, impairment Rs 1.0bn, software and licence amortisation Rs 4.9bn (licences Rs 0.9bn), lease (right-of-use) depreciation Rs 2.8bn and Rs 7.6bn of amortised dealer commissions and set-top boxes (contract costs, whose cash cost is already inside operating cash flow). So depreciation as reported overstates the capex needed to keep the network running; the calculator's range is Rs 31.9bn (average capex booked) to Rs 48.2bn, base Rs 46.3bn.

highlights.title: Capex below depreciation in 2024 and 2025, catching up in 2026
highlights.text: Capex booked was Rs 36.3bn in 2024 and Rs 27.5bn in 2025 against depreciation of Rs 45.8bn and Rs 48.2bn. In the nine months to September 2026 it was Rs 35.0bn (Rs 17.0bn a year earlier), about equal to depreciation of Rs 36.9bn, with only Rs 19.0bn paid in cash so far and Rs 15.7bn more contracted. This year's jump is mostly the 5G and fibre upgrade: largely keeping the network current rather than new capacity, so it is judged as maintenance more than growth.

highlights.title: Group changes
highlights.text: In October Dialog sold 20% of Digital Health for Rs 375m (Digital Health becomes an associate), and several small subsidiaries were merged into Digital Holdings Lanka on 30 September.

methodReadings.reading: 5.0x NAV. NAV understates a telecom, whose value is its network, spectrum and customers, so I give it no direct weight.

Excellent, but partly because the 2022 loss and high payouts shrank equity; the jump to 39% comes from profit nearly doubling (lower finance costs, margins up to 57%). With about 75% paid out, the profit kept supports about 7.8% growth a year.

2025 after-tax operating profit Rs 30.0bn on Rs 164.8bn of opening capital. Net reinvestment was slightly negative (capex Rs 20.6bn below depreciation, offset by Rs 18.3bn of working capital as payables were paid down), so on 2025 figures reinvestment supports no growth; 2026 capex is back at about depreciation.

Earnings yield 7.5% against a 12.24% government bond. With growth paid for out of profit, the P/E justified at a 14.7% cost of equity is about 6.5 / 8 / 10.6x; Dialog's own 2021–2025 average was about 7.6x.

Rs 0.70 a quarter (Rs 25.8bn a year). Covered about 1.4x by cash after maintenance capex over the 12 months to September (Rs 35.7bn), 1.08x in 2025: not at risk, but thin if working capital or 5G payments absorb cash.
Cash before interest after maintenance capex Rs 36bn (base), growing 5% with the capex that needs, at a 13.8% WACC, less Rs 56.7bn net debt. The price needs a WACC of about 10%.
On peer P/Es Dialog would be worth Rs 52–60. Peers' P/Es don't account for Sri Lanka's 12.24% bond yield or the capex growth needs, so I use them as a check, not a method.

models.name: Whole-company DCF (WACC, less net debt)
models.comment: Cash before interest after maintenance capex Rs 24 / 36 / 42bn, growing 2% / 5% / 7% for five years, then 3.5% / 4.5% / 5.5%, less the reinvestment growth needs at a 15% / 20% / 25% return on capital (after-tax operating profit Rs 32 / 39 / 42bn), at WACC 15.1% / 13.8% / 12.5%, less net debt Rs 56.7bn. Value after year 5: 54% / 66% / 75% (bull just under the 75% flag).

models.name: P/E method
models.comment: 2027 EPS of Rs 3.30 / 4.00 / 4.40 times 6.5 / 8 / 10.6: the forward P/E justified at the cost of equity when growth is paid for (payout = 1 − growth ÷ ROE, long-run ROE 20 / 25 / 30%). Base EPS equals the run-rate (latest quarter × 4 = Rs 4.00); bear 17.5% below it allows for exchange losses and a higher tax rate.

models.name: Dividend model
models.comment: Rs 2.40 / 2.80 / 3.20 a share, growing 2% / 5% / 7% for five years, then 3.5% / 4.5% / 5.5%, at the cost of equity 16.2% / 14.7% / 13.2%.

models.name: Residual income
models.comment: Book value Rs 9.99 (September); ROE falling from 40% to 20% / 25% / 30% over ten years; 75% payout; cost of equity 16.2% / 14.7% / 13.2%; after year ten the excess return grows at the long-run rate.

modelsNote: A steady cash generator, so the whole-company DCF carries full weight, alongside P/E, dividends and residual income. Growth check: assumed 2% / 5% / 7% against −1.4% supported by 2025 reinvestment × return on capital (7.8% on profit kept × ROE); all three are more than 2 points above, kept because 2025 reinvestment was held down by a one-off pay-down of payables and a capex dip, 2026 capex is back at depreciation with 5G spectrum bought and Rs 15.7bn contracted, revenue is growing 8% on the existing network, and the DCF still charges reinvestment (growth ÷ return on capital) for every point of growth. Assumptions were lowered by a point from 3% / 6% / 8%.

assumptions.label: Cash before interest after maintenance capex, start
Return on new capital (sets the reinvestment)

scenarios.common: Required return from CAPM with a country premium: risk-free 8.24% (12.24% bond less 4.0% default spread), mature premium 4.2% plus country premium 6.08%, beta 0.63 (provisional). Cost of debt 8.25% (interest paid ÷ average borrowings and leases, 2025), tax 22.2%, debt weight 10.9%. Start cash: bear is the calculator's 2025 figure (operating cash Rs 65.5bn + after-tax interest Rs 6.7bn − depreciation Rs 48.2bn); base and bull lean on the 12 months to September 2026 (operating cash Rs 82.0bn + after-tax interest Rs 4.9bn − Rs 46.3bn base maintenance ≈ Rs 40.5bn), less about Rs 4.5bn in the base for capex payables still to be paid. After-tax operating profit: trailing operating profit Rs 50.3bn taxed at 22% (base); bear at 30% in case the BOI tax deal ends and profit fades; bull at 16%, nearer the 2026 rate. Long-run reinvestment = growth ÷ return on capital (3.5/15 = 23%, 4.5/20 = 23%, 5.5/25 = 22%).

sensitivity.title: Whole-company DCF base case, Rs per share
sensitivity.note: Even the most generous corner (Rs 36.57) is well below today's price. Long-run growth matters little (Rs 26.4–28.5 for 3.5–5.5%). The price needs a WACC of about 10% in the base case.

buyPlan.note: About Rs 12,625 in total, against Rs 25,100 at Rs 50.20.
buyPlan.realism: Rs 24.40 needs about a 51% fall. The share last traded that low in 2025 (range Rs 11.40–32.50, close Rs 29.80); its 2026 low was Rs 30.10 (April–June) and the September-quarter low Rs 43.00. Not realistic this year without a market crash or a big rise in interest rates; even the first tier (Rs 28.70) is below this year's low.

higher: Interest rates falling: each point off WACC adds about Rs 4 a share in the base DCF.
A verified beta below 0.63 (e.g. Damodaran's emerging-markets telecom figure), or a lower country premium.
Evidence that new capex earns well above 20% (5G and home broadband lifting revenue growth above 8% while capex stays near depreciation).
The company disclosing maintenance capex well below depreciation (Rs 7.6bn of it is contract-cost amortisation and Rs 2.8bn lease depreciation).
Margins holding near 55–58%; a higher dividend (Rs 0.80+ a quarter) sustained without more borrowing.
lower: The BOI 2% revenue-tax deal ending: the 2025 report's goodwill note mentions an 'impending expiration of tax concession in year 2027' (p. 241); 30% tax on profit would cut after-tax profit sharply.
5G capex absorbing cash and cutting dividends, or borrowings rising to fund dividends.
Capex staying below depreciation for years (under-investment) while profit is reported as rising.
Another rupee crisis (2022: a Rs 33bn loss), or a higher bond yield.
Price competition from SLT-Mobitel and Hutch, or regulator-imposed tariff cuts.

notes.disclaimer: These are estimates from the 2025 annual report, the interim reports to June and September 2026, and earlier reports summarised in the research record. Figures for the 12 months to September 2026 are worked out from those reports. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.

Decision box.Verdict: Overpriced: about 75% above fair value of Rs 28.70.
Decision box.Expected yearly return at Rs 50.20: About −8% a year over three years: dividends 5.6% + growth 5% − about 17% a year if the price moved to fair value.
Decision box.Downside / upside: Bear case −65% (Rs 17.50); bull case −10% (Rs 45.20). Even the bull case is below today's price.
Decision box.What the price assumes: A WACC of about 10% in the base DCF, below the 12.24% government bond.
Decision box.Confidence: Medium: the methods give Rs 27–32 in the base case; the beta is provisional and maintenance capex uncertain (no company split).
Decision box.Margin of safety: Medium confidence: buy 15% below fair value (Rs 24.40), strong buy 25% below (Rs 21.50).

Business and moat.What it does: Mobile (78% of revenue in the nine months to September 2026), fixed and home broadband via Dialog Broadband Networks (15%), and pay TV via Dialog Television (7%). Also digital payments (eZ Cash), data centres and a finance company.
Business and moat.Market position: About 64% of mobile subscribers (19.6 million) after merging with Airtel Lanka in 2024; 22.3 million subscribers in total; largest pay-TV operator (1.6 million+). Competitors: SLT-Mobitel (state-controlled) and Hutch.
Business and moat.Moat: Wide: scale in a three-player market, the largest network, 5G spectrum won in December 2025 (100 MHz at 3.5 GHz, 200 MHz at 27 GHz), the strongest brand, and a tax deal competitors don't have.
Business and moat.Growth drivers: Data and home-broadband demand, price increases, 5G (1.5 million+ 5G users), enterprise and digital services. The low-margin international 'hubbing' business has been scaled down.
Business and moat.Customer and supplier concentration: Millions of retail customers; key suppliers are network-equipment vendors and the energy grid.
Business and moat.Tax advantage: The company pays a 2% revenue-based tax under its BOI agreement instead of 30% on profit; its broadband and TV subsidiaries pay 15% and 20%.
Business and moat.Segment profit, nine months 2026: Mobile Rs 30.6bn (Rs 22.4bn), fixed/broadband Rs 8.4bn (Rs 5.6bn), TV Rs 0.4bn (a Rs 0.3bn loss) of operating profit (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, note 3).

Management and governance.Ownership: Axiata Group (Malaysia) 73.75%, Bharti Airtel 10.36%, EPF 3.08% (2.90% earlier). Public float 15.85%, held by 29,367 shareholders (24,876 in December); foreign investors held 53% of the float at end-2025.
Management and governance.Track record: Delivered Rs 5.5bn of cost savings in 2025, completed the Airtel merger, cut USD debt from Rs 34.9bn to Rs 5.6bn, and paid above its 50% minimum payout. Rated OK.
Management and governance.Capital allocation: About 70–75% of profit paid out; capex raised for 5G; simplifying the group (five subsidiaries merged into Digital Holdings Lanka on 30 September 2026); sold 20% of Digital Health for Rs 375m in October 2026.
Management and governance.Related parties: Head-office charges to Axiata Rs 0.41bn in 2025 (Rs 1.1bn in 2024). A Rs 1.06bn impairment on money owed by affiliates in 2025: watch.
Management and governance.Auditor: Deloitte; clean opinion for 2025. Key audit matters: Rs 19.8bn of goodwill impairment testing, and mobile revenue recognition. The June and September 2026 interims were reviewed.
Management and governance.Director dealings: The CEO, Supun Weerasinghe, holds 4.26 million shares; no other directors hold shares directly.
Management and governance.Legal: A Rs 1.63bn customs dispute (Dialog Broadband Networks) is still in the Court of Appeal; argument refixed for 17 February 2027.

Accounting quality.Underlying earnings: Exchange losses net of gains of about Rs 0.75bn over the 12 months to September 2026 removed: underlying EPS about Rs 3.82 against reported Rs 3.74.
Accounting quality.Restatements: 2024 figures were restated in the 2025 accounts (December 2025 interim, note 17).
Accounting quality.Revaluations: None: property and equipment are carried at cost, so NAV isn't inflated.
Accounting quality.To check: The 'provision for other liabilities' (asset retirement obligations) jumped from Rs 4.96bn to Rs 9.14bn in January–March 2026 and was Rs 8.98bn in September, still with no explanation in the interim reports. Capex booked (Rs 35.0bn) far exceeds capex paid (Rs 19.0bn) in nine months, so cash flow is temporarily flattered.
Accounting quality.Depreciation make-up: Of Rs 48.2bn in 2025, Rs 7.6bn is amortisation of contract costs (dealer commissions, set-top boxes, routers) whose cash is spent inside operating cash flow, and Rs 2.8bn is lease depreciation; counting all of it as maintenance capex is conservative.
Accounting quality.Dividend cash vs declared: Nine months 2026: Rs 33.5bn of dividends paid in the cash flow statement against Rs 26.7bn in the company's changes in equity; the difference isn't explained.

Peer and history comparison.Sri Lanka Telecom (SLTL.N0000): P/E about 15–18x, P/B about 1.5x, ROE about 11%, dividend yield about 1%, EV/EBITDA about 5x (web data from June 2026; dates vary).
Peer and history comparison.Dialog's own history: Year-end P/E 3.7–13.2x in 2021–2025 (average about 7.6x excluding 2022); P/B 1.0–3.0x. Today's 13.3x and 5.1x are at the top of its range.
Peer and history comparison.Reading: Cheap against peers on P/E, expensive against its own history and against Sri Lankan bond yields.

Sri Lanka checks.Interest rates: Watch: policy rate raised to 8.75% in May 2026; 10-year bond about 12.4%. A yield stock like Dialog loses value when rates rise.
Sri Lanka checks.Rupee: Watch: rupee down 6.7% against the dollar this year (6 Nov). Network equipment, energy and roaming are dollar-linked; dollar debt is now small (Rs 5.6bn). Exchange loss Rs 0.92bn in the September quarter.
Sri Lanka checks.Tax and regulation: Risk: the 2% revenue tax depends on the BOI agreement; telecom levies and tariff approvals by the regulator (TRCSL); the 2027 budget was being finalised in November 2026.
Sri Lanka checks.Dependence on the state: OK: customers are households and businesses, not the government.
Sri Lanka checks.Energy and weather: Watch: high energy costs from the Middle East conflict; Cyclone Ditwah disrupted the network in late 2025.
Sri Lanka checks.Liquidity: OK: one of the most traded shares on the CSE; 500 shares (about Rs 25,100) are easy to buy or sell.
Sri Lanka checks.Free float and control: Watch: only 15.85% free float; Axiata controls the company.
Sri Lanka checks.Catalysts: Ex-dividend Rs 0.70 on 20 November (paid 10 December); full-year 2026 results due early February 2027; 5G rollout and capex payments; any change in Axiata's stake.
Sri Lanka checks.ESG: OK: no major controversies found; energy use and carbon footprint are the main issues.
Sri Lanka checks.Going concern / audit: OK: clean audit opinion, AAA(lka) rating from Fitch.

Crisis stress test (2022-style).Scenario: Rupee falls 40%, interest rates up 10 points, demand down 5%.
Crisis stress test (2022-style).Likely effect (rough estimate): Exchange loss on dollar debt about Rs 4bn; extra interest about Rs 6bn a year on Rs 64bn of local borrowings; higher dollar costs. Profit could fall from about Rs 34bn to about Rs 15–20bn.
Crisis stress test (2022-style).Survival: Survives comfortably: low debt, AAA rating and a strong parent. Dividends would probably be cut, and the share price could halve (in 2022 it fell to Rs 8.50 and the P/E collapsed).

Portfolio fit.Cost of 500 shares: About Rs 25,100 now; about Rs 12,200 at the buy price.
Portfolio fit.Overlap: None with other companies on the site; it is the site's only telecom.
Portfolio fit.Note: Shown for information, not as advice on how much to hold.

Broker view.HNB Stockbrokers (9 Nov 2026): Moderate buy, target Rs 55, against my fair value of Rs 28.70.
Broker view.Why we differ: The broker's target is close to peer P/E multiples (about 15x). My methods discount at a 13.8% WACC / 14.7% cost of equity because Sri Lankan bonds yield 12.24%, and they charge for the capex growth needs. If rates fall, the gap narrows.

Investment case and sell rules.Why own it: Dominant market leader with a wide moat, high returns, strong cash flow, low debt and a 5–7% dividend.
Investment case and sell rules.The case is broken if: Market share falls clearly below 60%; the BOI tax deal ends; 5G capex forces a dividend cut; or a rupee crisis returns.
Investment case and sell rules.Sell triggers: Price more than 30% above fair value (above Rs 37.30: today's price is above this); the case breaks; or a clearly better opportunity appears.

fullText:
Summary: Dialog Axiata (DIAL.N0000) is Sri Lanka's dominant telecom company: about 64% of mobile users, the largest broadband and pay-TV operator, the first 5G network, low debt and a AAA local credit rating. Results are strong: nine-month EPS Rs 3.10 against Rs 1.62, trailing EPS about Rs 3.74, borrowings down to Rs 64bn. This full redo (requested as /redo DIAL full, 14 November 2026) re-read the 2025 annual report and the June and September 2026 interims, filled in the capex, depreciation and working-capital figures the record lacked, and applies the new required-return rule. A beta of 0.63 gives a cost of equity of 14.7% and a WACC of 13.8%, lower than the hand-set 16.5% used before, so fair value rises from Rs 25.50 to about Rs 28.70. At Rs 50.20 (CSE close, 13 November 2026) the price is about 75% above that and implies a WACC of about 10%, below the 12.24% government bond. I'd buy at up to about Rs 24.40 and treat under Rs 21.50 as a strong buy. The business tests still pass 3 of 4, so it stays on the watch list.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 50.20 (CSE close, 13 November 2026). It traded between Rs 43.00 and Rs 49.90 in July–September and Rs 30.10–48.40 in April–June; it closed 2025 at Rs 29.80.
September 2026 quarter (reviewed): revenue Rs 48.54bn (up 6.2%), gross margin 58.4%, operating profit Rs 13.47bn, profit Rs 9.24bn (up 62%), EPS Rs 1.00 (Rs 0.62), finance costs down 42%, exchange loss Rs 0.92bn, third interim dividend Rs 0.70.
Nine months to September 2026: revenue Rs 144.1bn (up 8.2%), operating profit Rs 39.3bn (Rs 27.6bn), profit Rs 28.5bn, EPS Rs 3.10 (Rs 1.62), operating cash flow Rs 67.1bn after Rs 4.2bn of interest paid, depreciation and amortisation Rs 36.9bn, capex booked Rs 35.0bn but paid Rs 19.0bn.
Balance sheet, 30 September 2026: borrowings Rs 64.1bn (Rs 76.5bn in December, Rs 107.7bn at end-2024), cash Rs 20.6bn, net debt including leases Rs 56.7bn (0.58x EBITDA), NAV Rs 9.99.
2025 (audited): revenue Rs 179.6bn, operating profit Rs 38.6bn, EBITDA Rs 86.0bn, profit Rs 20.8bn, EPS Rs 2.26, ROE 23%, tax rate 22.2%, dividend Rs 1.50; depreciation, impairment and amortisation Rs 48.2bn; capex booked Rs 27.5bn, paid Rs 27.7bn; working capital up Rs 18.3bn; interest paid Rs 8.6bn.

Required return
Cost of equity = risk-free 8.24% (12.24% bond less a 4.0% default spread) + beta 0.63 × (4.2% mature premium + 6.08% country premium) = 14.7%; bear 16.2%, bull 13.2%. Cost of debt 8.25% (interest paid Rs 8.57bn ÷ average borrowings and leases); after 22.2% tax, 6.4%. Debt is 10.9% of market value, so WACC is 15.1% / 13.8% / 12.5%.
The beta is provisional. Damodaran's emerging-markets telecom beta couldn't be read in this run, so his US Telecom Services unlevered beta (0.38) stood in; relevered at Dialog's low debt it is 0.42. Local 5-year betas from web-search extracts were 0.66, 0.48 and 0.63 (median 0.63). The rule takes the higher, 0.63. It should be rechecked in January 2027.

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
Whole-company DCF | 10.2 | 27.4 | 49.8 | 26.7
P/E | 21.4 | 32.0 | 46.6 | 31.7
Dividend model | 18.1 | 27.9 | 43.6 | 28.1
Residual income | 20.3 | 27.8 | 40.7 | 28.1
Average | 17.5 | 28.8 | 45.2 | 28.7

Reinvestment, capex and growth
- Maintenance capex: Dialog gives no split. The calculator's range is Rs 48.2bn (depreciation as reported, bear), Rs 46.3bn (less impairment and licence amortisation, base) and Rs 31.9bn (average capex booked 2024–2025, bull). Depreciation includes Rs 7.6bn of amortised dealer commissions and set-top boxes, whose cash is already spent inside operating cash flow, and Rs 2.8bn of lease depreciation, so the bear and base figures are conservative.
- Cash before interest and growth spending: 2025 operating cash flow Rs 65.5bn plus Rs 6.7bn of after-tax interest (Dialog puts interest paid in operating cash flow) = Rs 72.2bn, less maintenance = Rs 24.0bn / 25.9bn / 40.3bn. 2025 was held down by an Rs 18.3bn working-capital outflow as payables were paid down. Over the 12 months to September 2026 the same sum is about Rs 40.5bn in the base case. The DCF starts from Rs 24 / 36 / 42bn.
- Capex below depreciation: Rs 36.3bn booked against Rs 45.8bn in 2024, and Rs 27.5bn against Rs 48.2bn in 2025. In 2026 booked capex is back to about depreciation (Rs 35.0bn against Rs 36.9bn in nine months), mostly the 5G and fibre upgrade. That is mostly keeping the network current, so I judge it as maintenance more than growth. Watch that paid capex catches up (Rs 19.0bn paid so far).
- Growth check: on 2025 figures reinvestment was −Rs 2.2bn, so reinvestment × return on capital (18.2%) supports −1.4% growth. Profit kept × ROE gives 7.8%. Assumed growth is 2% / 5% / 7%, a point lower than before, and all three are more than 2 points above the capex-based figure. They are kept for four reasons: 2025 reinvestment was depressed by a one-off pay-down of payables and a capex dip; 2026 capex is back at depreciation, with the 5G spectrum bought and Rs 15.7bn contracted; revenue is growing about 8% on the existing network through pricing and data use; and the DCF still charges growth ÷ return on capital in reinvestment every year.
- Long-run growth is 3.5% / 4.5% / 5.5%, below the 12.24% bond and below WACC. It needs 23% / 23% / 22% of after-tax operating profit reinvested.
- Earnings run-rate: latest quarter × 4 = Rs 4.00 (trailing 12 months Rs 3.74). The base 2027 EPS is Rs 4.00, at the run-rate. The bear case (Rs 3.30) allows for exchange losses and a higher tax rate.
- Dividend cover: cash after maintenance capex covered dividends paid 1.08x in 2025 and about 1.4x over the 12 months to September, so the dividend is not flagged as at risk.
- R&D: not disclosed, so no adjustment.
- Ratio checks: beta 0.63, cost of equity 14.7% and WACC 13.8% are within range. Cost of debt 8.25% is at the bottom of the house range (bond − 4 points) because part of the debt was cheaper dollar loans and short-term bank lines. ROE of 39% is a one-year jump from profit nearly doubling on a small equity base, so the residual income model fades it to 25%. Net debt/EBITDA is 0.58x. Value after year 5 in the DCF is 54% / 66% / 75%, with the bull case right at the flag.

Assumptions
DCF: start cash Rs 24 / 36 / 42bn and after-tax operating profit Rs 32 / 39 / 42bn (trailing operating profit Rs 50.3bn at 30% / 22% / 16% tax; 30% in the bear case in case the BOI revenue-tax deal ends), growing 2% / 5% / 7% for five years, then 3.5% / 4.5% / 5.5%. Return on new capital is 15% / 20% / 25%. Discounted at WACC 15.1% / 13.8% / 12.5%, less net debt Rs 56.7bn.
P/E: 2027 EPS Rs 3.30 / 4.00 / 4.40 at 6.5 / 8 / 10.6x, the forward P/E justified at the cost of equity when growth is paid for.
Dividends: Rs 2.40 / 2.80 / 3.20, growing 2% / 5% / 7% then 3.5% / 4.5% / 5.5%.
Residual income: book value Rs 9.99, ROE from 40% to 20% / 25% / 30% over ten years.

What changed in this redo
- Record rebuilt from the CSE downloads. 2025 and 2024 reinvestment figures (depreciation split, capex booked, impairment, licence amortisation, working capital, acquisitions, operating profit, tax rate, equity, borrowings, leases, interest paid) were added, and the 2025 cash-flow page reference was corrected to p. 209.
- Required return: beta 0.63, cost of equity 14.7% (was 16.5% set by hand), WACC 13.8%.
- DCF: now the whole company at WACC less net debt, starting from cash before interest. Weighted Rs 22.6 → Rs 26.7.
- P/E: justified multiples 6.5 / 8 / 10.6x at the new cost of equity (were 6 / 7.5 / 9.5x). Weighted Rs 29.3 → Rs 31.7.
- Dividend model Rs 26.2 → Rs 28.1; residual income Rs 23.9 → Rs 28.1.
- Fair value Rs 25.50 → Rs 28.70, buy Rs 21.70 → Rs 24.40, strong buy Rs 19.10 → Rs 21.50.

Peers and history
Sri Lanka Telecom trades at roughly 15–18x earnings and Asian telecoms at about 16x; on those multiples Dialog would be worth Rs 52–60. But its own P/E averaged about 7.6x in 2021–2025, and its 7.5% earnings yield is well below the 12.24% government bond. HNB Stockbrokers rates it a moderate buy with a Rs 55 target.

Risks to watch
Interest rates, the rupee, the BOI tax deal (the 2025 goodwill note mentions an impending expiry of a tax concession in 2027), 5G capex payments, capex lagging depreciation, energy costs, a 15.85% free float, and the unexplained Rs 4bn rise in asset-retirement provisions. In a 2022-style crisis it would survive but cut dividends, and the price could halve.

500-share plan
200 shares up to Rs 28.70, 150 up to Rs 24.40 and 150 up to Rs 21.50: average about Rs 25.25, about Rs 12,625 in total. Rs 24.40 needs about a 51% fall. The share was last that low in 2025, and this year's low was Rs 30.10, so the plan is unlikely to fill without a market crash or a big rise in rates.

Sell rules
If you already hold Dialog: the price is above the sell trigger (30% above fair value, Rs 37.30). The business case itself is intact.

Business tests: 3 of 4 passed (returns, debt and cash; it fails steady profit because of the 2022 loss). So it's a good business at a high price: watch list, unchanged.
